copy.copy_1: Keeping the center anchored to the low post opens more outside shot opportunities for your other four players.
copy.copy_2: Ball handlers have plenty of great options. Shoot the outside shot, drive to the basket, hit the cutter on his way to the basket, or feed low post player.
copy.copy_3: Great opportunity to get your PF involved in the outside shooting game if your PF has a high SH attribute.

copy.copy_1: The best motion offense for creating drive opportunities.
copy.copy_2: Relies more on player agility and good decision making as there are very few screens in the motion loop. Players need to be able to create their own plays.
copy.copy_3: Inside shot opportunities are limited to drives to the basket and passing to a cutter. There are no post up opportunities.

copy.copy_1: A very focused offensive set. Keeps your PF & C down low, and your PG, SG, & SF outisde.
copy.copy_2: Continual screens set for the players as they cut from mid lane to the outside wing. Great if you have great screeners and great athletes who can leverage the screen, then catch and shoot quickly.
copy.copy_3: Not much diversity of action. Your players will simply need to out-execute as the defense will have a high chance of picking up on the repetitive motion pattern.

copy.copy_1: Gets the ball to your SF with an opportunity to leverage his athleticism and decision making ability.
copy.copy_2: Relies heavily on the screening ability of your big men.
copy.copy_3: While the SF is the focus, the PG has the opportunity to make a quick read to the SG on the upper wing if the opportunity is there.

copy.copy_1: Multiple step and longer duration requires multiple players to execute flawlessly.
copy.copy_2: The double screen for your SG will create some amazing looks for the 3-point shot from the wing.
copy.copy_3: The SG has the option to drive to the basket if the outside shot is well defended. Particularly because the low post on his side is not occupied.

copy.copy_1: The bread & butter play of your offense. PF sets a screen to get the C a strong look on the block.
copy.copy_2: PG screening for the SG on the upper wing creates a great alternate opportunity for an outside shot if the low post pass is not there.
copy.copy_3: The entry pass going to your SF gets your most versatile player the ball at one of the most opportunistic spots in the half court offense. He has a low post pass opportunity, outside shot pass opportunity, or he can create his own opportunity with a shot or drive.

copy.copy_1: Continuously screening to get your PF a low-post shot attempt.
copy.copy_2: PG/SG/SF rotate screening for each other at the top of the key. The ball handler coming off the screen has the option to pass to the PF on the low post, or take the shot himself.
copy.copy_3: Very few variability options -- if this play gets disrupted, most offenses will find it challenging to effectively recover.

copy.copy_1: Sets up your PF for a quick mid-range jump shot.
copy.copy_2: Particularly effective if you have a wide-bodied C setting the screen for your PF.
copy.copy_3: If the jump shot isn't there, it's on your PF to create an opportunity with the drive and/or pass.

copy.copy_1: Great at isolating the PF for an open 3-pointer from the corner.
copy.copy_2: The SG has multiple read options. While the PF is the primary, he can also dish to the SF cutting to the basket, shoot the shot himself off the drive, or kick out to the PG on the opposite wing.
copy.copy_3: A strong screen by the C is what makes this play go.
